details.label: Summary
details.text: Ongoing developing severe storm cluster will probably be maintained at least a few more hours, and its possible it could approach areas near/west of Greater Omaha by 5-6 AM CDT, accompanied by the risk for damaging wind gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Though embedded within modest westerly deep-layer mean flow on the order of 20 kt, the ongoing intense supercell/compact cluster has been maintaining a southeastward propagation near 40 kts. This has been accompanied by an increase in severe gusts to the north/northwest of Ainsworth and O'Neill. On its current track, it appears likely to approach areas near/west of the Greater Omaha vicinity by 10-11Z. While there does appear potential to maintain continuing inflow of seasonably moist air supportive of sizable CAPE, convection continues to propagate into an environment with increased mid-level inhibition, with somewhat limited forcing for ascent. Activity will probably have to continue to grow upscale in the near term, accompanied by a substantively expanding and strengthening surface cold pool to provide continuing support for maintenance. This remains a bit uncertain, but appears possible. Regardless, a risk for severe winds will likely persist for at least a few more hours, requiring a new severe weather watch issuance

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A maturing bow will continue to yield a risk for higher-end wind potential over the next 1-2 hours as it moves into northern portions of NE

details.label: Summary
details.text: A maturing bow will continue to yield a risk for higher-end wind potential over the next 1-2 hours as it moves into northern portions of NE

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest radar imagery from KFSD/KUDX shows a potent cluster evolving into a maturing bow along the NE/SD border with echo tops increasing in the past 30 minutes to 60 kft. The airmass remains very unstable per RAP forecast soundings (around 4000 J/kg MUCAPE) with modest lower to mid-level flow (20-25 kt) increasing to 60 kt around 250 mb. This thermodynamic/kinematic environment will continue to strongly favor severe gusts and a continuation of the mature phase of the bow echo through at least 2-3am CDT. Recently measured gusts in the 90-95 mph range in southern SD are indicative of the higher-end wind potential

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...85-100 MPH
